newsitem.title: MEXICO: Reebok to invest $5 mln in Mexico plant.
newsitem.headline: Reebok to invest $5 mln in Mexico plant.

text.p: Reebok International Ltd, the athletic shoe giant, said Monday it would invest $5 million to build a new plant in the central Mexican state of Guanajato.

"This is the first Reebok plant that is not in Asia and represents a big opportunity for Mexico to produce and export to the United States," Andre Bruere, director general of the company in Mexico, told Reuters.
The plant in the city of Juventino Rosas, expected to begin operations in May 1997, will produce 1.5 million pairs of shoes a year and generate 1,000 jobs, Bruere said.
Interviewed in Leon at the National Shoe Fair, which concludes on Tuesday, Bruere said Reebok chose Guanajato state over other sites in Zacatecas, Morelos and Hidalgo states.
Guanajato won out in part because the state government will help Reebok find qualified labor and expedite permits for the plant, Bruere said.
"The challenge is to prove that we are capable of producing in Mexico and that it (Mexico) can be a base for the export market in the rest of Latin America," he said.
He said Reebok has 25 plants in Asia with a production of 88 million pairs of shoes per year.
"The idea of the new Reebok plant in Mexico is that 50 percent of production will be destined for the domestic market and 50 percent for the export market," Bruere said.
Reebok imported one million pairs of shoes in Mexico in 1996, he said.
"Demand in Mexico has fallen a lot since the crisis, but the capacity of its workforce is an impulse for us to produce shoes here," Bruere said.

He said the company faces a serious problem of counterfeit Reeboks hitting the market, which he hoped would be overcome in Mexico by producing a superior shoe at a more accessible price. "The other road we have and one we have taken is legal action, in which we have a lot of support from the Mexican authorities.
